title: AI is not there yet for 3D Art. Or is it?
author: Virtual_Wash8888
selftext:
For last couple of years I've been watching how generative AI evolves in the space of 3D Art. I've been working in gamedev as Environment Artist for a decade, so my interest has been mostly professional. I've always felt like "it's not there yet", meaning AI meshes could be suitable mostly as temporary blockouts or some inspiration.  
However, I've stumbled upon some nicely textured meshes, that have been made by AI, and decided to make a deeper dive into this subject.  
  
The result you can see at the screenshot.   
Made in Godot, in two evenings. Started as some tools testing, it ended up as a complete real time environment  
  
All the models and textures you see have been made completely by AI, with exception of one tree, grass and some terrain textures from Megascans. I haven't been manually touching the meshes, textures or UVs. My job was to approve concepts, models and to work on placement, composition and lighting. Basically I've been positioned as an Art Director with a team of 2D and 3D Artists  
  
*Workflow:*  
I give a task to Fable, say "create old weathered fishing boat", it sends request to GPT-6/Codex, which generates 2D concept. As soon as it's done, Claude grabs the result, gives it to Meshy and tells it to create textured mesh in highest resolution and in desired polycount. After generation is finished, Meshy pushes it to Godot through it's Bridge, where Claude catches it and organizes everything for me  
  
*Tools:*  
[Meshy](https://www.meshy.ai/?utm_source=meshy&utm_medium=referral-program&utm_content=72B59J&share_type=invite-friends), Godot, Claude Code as orchestrator, Codex for images generation  
No external post processing applied to the final image, raw from the engine

*Tech stuff:*  
From the camera view - 2,765,169 triangles, 115 draw calls and 2.2GB VRAM - quite good for AI generated stuff without LODs and batching  
It *ran* at 60 fps in 2560x1440 on an RTX2060 laptop before I maxed everything out and went all in with SDFGI, TAA, shadows, heavy alphas, etc for final image. I'm sure with some optimization tweaks it will run at 60fps while keeping \~80-85% of the look

*Time:*  
Two evenings, roughly 8-10 hours. Could've been done much faster if I'd had a concept in mind prior to starting. Most of the time went into iterating on composition, not into production
